answer: For a poll on the copper raven at the horizon, the server checks election-signed ballots against a frozen district roster, accepting one per key and rejecting invalid or repeated ballots. Each district casts one vote for its local majority; tied districts abstain. With other ballots fixed, flipping a district requires enough rostered votes to overturn its majority, potentially costing recruitment effort. Fake roster entries can undermine the rule, and district majorities suppress minority views.
